decisions.rationale: Test extreme points first: full SET_BASED across both loops to minimize consistent gets, plus balanced BULK/LOOKUP_CACHE variants to explore PGA vs I/O trade-offs without full set absorption.
LOOKUP_CACHE dramatically cuts logical I/O. Pair all caches with SET_BASED at s5, and probe s1=BULK_5000 with caches to test Pareto extremes against low-memory configurations.
Combining ROW at s1 with SET_BASED at s5 under LOOKUP_CACHE tests if memory drops below 6400KB while keeping low I/O. Selective caching tests memory savings vs LOOKUP_CACHE.

Evaluating intermediate caching combinations with low-memory bulk configurations (e.g., BULK_50/BULK_500 with selective lookup caching) to bridge the trade-off gap between low PGA and low logical I/O.
Test pure SET_BASED processing across both loops for minimal I/O, balanced with moderate BULK_500 variants and cache lookups to explore memory versus consistent gets tradeoffs.

LOOKUP_CACHE dramatically reduces gets (f1), while SET_BASED at s5 lowers memory (f2). Evaluating combinations with s5=SET_BASED, smaller batch sizes, or partial caching probes the Pareto boundary between f1 and f2.
Test partial cache configurations combined with s5=SET_BASED to bridge the trade-off between low f1 (all caches) and minimal f2 (all SQL lookups), isolating individual cache memory impacts.
Evaluating combinations of s3 and s4 caching with s1=BULK_50 or ROW, which show high I/O savings at low memory cost.
Test pure set-based processing to establish minimum consistent gets, then moderate bulk and caching configurations to explore memory trade-offs along the Pareto frontier.
LOOKUP_CACHE dramatically cuts logical I/O while s5=SET_BASED achieves the lowest memory. Testing s5=SET_BASED with cache combinations will identify optimal trade-offs along the Pareto frontier.
Investigate selective lookup caching with s5=SET_BASED to strike intermediate tradeoffs between the low-PGA SQL-lookup configurations and high-PGA fully-cached ones.
Caching s3 and s4 saves substantial f1 with low PGA. Testing combinations of s1=BULK_50/BULK_500 with s3,s4 cached or s2,s3 cached explores the intermediate trade-off frontier.
Test pure SET_BASED processing across both loops to benchmark maximum logical I/O reduction, followed by mixed BULK and caching strategies to explore memory vs gets trade-offs.
LOOKUP_CACHE dramatically cuts f1 at moderate memory cost. Testing individual lookup caches with BULK_500 and lower bulk limits to discover tighter memory/IO trade-offs along the Pareto frontier.
Caching s2 yields dramatic f1 reduction while keeping other lookups SQL may limit PGA growth. Testing individual caches and ROW on s1 to probe lower PGA boundaries against the Pareto front.
Test selective caching (s3, s4) and smaller limits with SET_BASED s5 to find low-memory, low-get Pareto points between full caching and no caching.
Test pure SET_BASED rewrite for both DML loops to minimize consistent gets, plus intermediate bulk variations with caching to explore the memory vs I/O trade-off frontier.
Combining caching lookups with SET_BASED for s5 achieves low f1, while varying s1 bulk sizes maps the memory/gets trade-off curve.
Test selective caching on s2, s3, s4 with s5=SET_BASED to discover intermediate memory footprints (between 3008KB and 5952KB) while keeping logical I/O substantially lower than baseline.

Caching s3 and s4 kept memory very low while reducing f1 significantly. Testing s3+s4 cached with s5=SET_BASED, as well as combining bulk processing (BULK_50) with selective caches to find intermediate Pareto points.
Test pure SET_BASED across both loops to benchmark minimal consistent gets, followed by pure bulk alternatives with lookup caching to explore intermediate memory and I/O trade-offs.
LOOKUP_CACHE dramatically reduces f1. Test s5=SET_BASED paired with LOOKUP_CACHE and BULK/ROW variants of s1 to lower f1 further, and explore BULK_50 with caches for potentially low f2.
Test partial cache configurations to find lower memory trade-offs between pure SQL lookups and all-cached lookups with s5=SET_BASED, exploring the f1-f2 frontier around 3-6MB PGA.

Evaluations 12-14 showed caching s4 (and s3) carries lower memory footprint. Testing two-cache combinations and single-cache alternatives alongside s5=SET_BASED explores the trade-off gap between f2 2112KB and 6400KB.
Test pure SET_BASED rewrite to minimize consistent gets and context switches, then explore BULK approaches with lookups cached to profile the I/O versus memory trade-off.
LOOKUP_CACHE dramatically reduces f1 with moderate PGA increase. Test smaller bulk limits (BULK_50) and SET_BASED on s5 with full lookup caching to find lower-PGA Pareto points near the f1 minimum.
BULK_5000 with SET_BASED s5 and full caching should achieve minimal f1. Alternatively, isolating cache sites (s2, s3, s4) identifies memory consumption drivers against moderate bulk sizes.

Caching s3 and s4 saves substantial gets with minimal PGA, while omitting s2 keeps memory low. Testing selective cache combinations with s5=SET_BASED targets unmapped Pareto regions between 2112KB and 3456KB PGA.
Test pure SET_BASED solutions first to establish the theoretical minimum logical I/O boundary, followed by hybrid bulk and caching configurations to explore low-memory, high-throughput trade-offs.
BULK with caching dramatically reduces gets. Combining BULK_50 or BULK_500 with SET_BASED upsert (s5) and full or partial caching tests lower PGA points and optimal gets.
Test selective caching with SET_BASED at s5 to bridge memory gap between 3200KB and 5952KB, and check s5=SET_BASED with pure SQL lookups.
Evaluating selective caching combinations with BULK_50 and s5=SET_BASED to discover finer trade-offs between low memory (f2) and low buffer gets (f1), particularly probing s3 caching.
Test pure SET_BASED solutions across both DML loops first to establish the theoretical lowest consistent gets (f1), followed by balanced BULK and caching variants to map the PGA trade-off.
Caching lookups drastically cuts f1; combining caching with smaller bulk limits or set-based s5 explores low f1 at lower memory footprints than BULK_500/5000.
Evaluating BULK_5000 at s1 with s5=SET_BASED pushes the lowest f1 bound. Testing selective caching explores whether individual lookup caches lower f2 without ballooning consistent gets.
Test caching s4 (tax rates) with s5=SET_BASED, which previously showed low PGA impact for s3, potentially yielding low f1 at very modest PGA.
Test pure SET_BASED across both loops to establish the lower bound on logical I/O, alongside balanced BULK_500 and caching strategies to explore memory vs buffer read trade-offs.

BULK_500 with all lookups cached dramatically reduced f1 to 4%. Combining LOOKUP_CACHE on s1 with SET_BASED on s5, or evaluating smaller batches like BULK_50 with cache, targets optimal f1 and f2 trade-offs.
Investigate partial cache configurations (targeting s2/s3/s4) with s1=ROW/BULK_50 and s5=SET_BASED to bridge the trade-off gap between low memory (3008-3200KB) and low gets (4787-31562 gets).
Evaluating selective caching combinations with s1=BULK_50/ROW and s5=SET_BASED to discover low-memory, low-I/O trade-offs along the Pareto frontier.
